notes: Paper derives bounds on hidden photon kinetic mixing parameter χ from two independent methods: (1) Solar energy loss argument (T-Lifetime and L-Lifetime bounds), requiring hidden photon luminosity < solar luminosity L☉ = 3.83×10²⁶ W; (2) CAST helioscope non-observation of converted photons in 0.5–15 keV window with flux limit Φ_CAST < 10⁻⁵ cm⁻² s⁻¹ keV⁻¹. The energy loss bound dominates for m_γ' ∈ [1 eV, 295 eV] via resonant production (χ ≲ 10⁻¹⁴ at m_γ' ~ 10 eV). CAST provides strongest constraints at low masses (3 meV < m_γ' < 1 eV) and extends bounds to ~40 keV. Data points extracted from Fig. 6 (Helioscope and Lifetime curves) by reading approximate values at key mass scales. The paper explicitly states bounds are valid for 3 meV < m_γ' < 40 keV. Resonant production in the range 1–295 eV significantly improves bounds over previous work [35,36]. Weak mixing condition χ²m⁴_γ'/(π_a - m²_γ') ≪ 1 verified throughout. Paper does not assume local DM density (this is a stellar/helioscope bound, not a haloscope). | selector: text (sole candidate)
